### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-odata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **61** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-odata/README.md`, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/package.json`, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via pageSize (symbol, a field of const object ODataDriverConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via pageSize (symbol, a field of const object ODataDriverConfigSchema))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via keyValue (symbol, a method of const object odataV2Dialect; a method of interface ODataDialect))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via fieldTypes (symbol, a field of interface ObjectDeclaration))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-odata/README.md`, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/package.json`, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 412908cf9e982d86307504fa6e860111c046926a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `39262b3e630e444c8259fd37d92f13ed1dd442d7` — the merge of head `667660add518c9a9e904cf24836ea68dfb09b5a3` into base `412908cf9e982d86307504fa6e860111c046926a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 39262b3e630e444c8259fd37d92f13ed1dd442d7 && git checkout 39262b3e630e444c8259fd37d92f13ed1dd442d7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 412908cf9e982d86307504fa6e860111c046926a 667660add518c9a9e904cf24836ea68dfb09b5a3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 412908cf9e982d86307504fa6e860111c046926a && git merge --no-ff 667660add518c9a9e904cf24836ea68dfb09b5a3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 412908cf9e982d86307504fa6e860111c046926a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 412908cf9e982d86307504fa6e860111c046926a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `667660add518c9a9e904cf24836ea68dfb09b5a3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts + packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts (`typeVocabulary`, `generateObjectDraft`, `validateObjectUsing`, read on `main`), packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/external-object-draft-odata-metadata.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/dialect-v2.ts (`parseCsdlV2` property types, `readValue` / `writeValue` for `Edm.DateTime` and `Edm.Time`), packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts (`introspectSchema` dialect string, `readValues`), packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/config.ts, docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md §4.6 (read, not changed)

Inputs read: card #28125 (body and all three comments: triage 6524734159, claim 6524866087, os-dev-report 6526649009), PR #28177 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at merge-base `062a2323`), and the 43 check-runs on this head. Reviewed at 2026-10-30T15:47Z.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ODataDriverConfigSchema.version`: `z.literal('4.0')` → `z.enum(['4.0', '2.0'])`, default `4.0` unchanged** (config.ts, outside `hits`, named because it drives the declared arm). A second accepted value of an authored datasource config field: accept-set widening; `Metadata-protocol: added` is the right kind. Right.
2. **`DIALECT_ALIASES.odata` gains `edm.datetime` → `datetime` and `edm.time` → `time`** (the `hits` file). Both answered `unknown` on `main`. The consequences at the published `canonicalizeSqlType` / `suggestFieldTypeForSqlType` / `isCompatible` face, each named:
   - `suggestFieldTypeForSqlType('Edm.DateTime' | 'Edm.Time', 'odata')`: `undefined` → `'datetime'` / `'time'`. A draft stops typing those columns `text` with an "unrecognised remote type" review note. Right.
   - `isCompatible(…, 'datetime' | 'time', 'odata')`: `false` → `true`. Gate 2 stops refusing a `datetime` field over `Edm.DateTime` and a `time` field over `Edm.Time` as a `type_mismatch` error. Widening. Right.
   - `isCompatible('Edm.DateTime', 'date', 'odata')`: `false` → `'lossy'` (the `datetime` row's lossy set). Gate 2 moves from an error to a warning, which matches the driver's `readValue` reading the UTC date alone under a field declared `date`; `lossy` is the honest word, because an `Edm.DateTime` column may carry a time of day the field drops. Widening. Right.
   - `isCompatible('Edm.DateTime' | 'Edm.Time', 'text' | 'json', 'odata')`: `'lossy'` → `false`. The `unknown` row's permissive text/json fallback no longer applies once the type is recognised. At the function face this is a narrowing. In a deployment it is reachable only through a dialect-`odata` introspection that names those two types, and on `main` none can exist: `version: '2.0'` was refused at boot, and CSDL 4.0 declares neither name. The deployed accept set therefore only widens, and the arm `yes (widening)` stands; it is the same shape as #27745, which introduced the whole `odata` arm (every EDM name moved out of `unknown`) under `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The sentence "Nothing that passed before fails now" in the PR body and changeset is true of deployed objects and overstated at the bare function face; it is prose and is noted here, not judged.
   - Dialect reach: the driver reports `dialect: odata-2.0` (odata-driver.ts `introspectSchema`); the service's `typeVocabulary` on `main` folds `odata` and every `odata-*` to the matrix's `odata` arm, so the two aliases reach the first consumer without a service change. Verified in the cited code; the head's service-datasource test pins the dialect string and the drafted `datetime`.
3. **`ODataDialect` gains four optional members** (`readValue`, `writeValue`, `keyValue`, `updateRequest`; dialect.ts, outside `hits`). Additive on an exported interface; `odataV4Dialect` implements none; the driver falls back to v4 behaviour when one is absent, so an out-of-repo dialect still compiles and behaves as before. Right.
4. **New exports `odataV2Dialect`, `parseCsdlV2`** from the driver's index; `parseCsdlV4`'s v1/EDMX refusal text is reworded (the v4 suite's pin still matches, per the diff). Additive. Right.
5. **No governed path** in the file list; docs/adr/0015 §4.6 is not touched and does not need to be: its text says the `odata` arm "maps the EDM primitive types an OData service's `$metadata` declares, except `Edm.Duration` and the `Edm.Geography*` / `Edm.Geometry*` families", which is version-neutral, and the two additions bring the table closer to that sentence rather than away from it. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28125-driver-odata-v2-dialect.md`: `@objectstack/driver-odata: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`.
- Level follows the kind alone (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3): a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves. `added` is right for the driver (a new accepted value of `version`), so `minor` on both moved packages is what the rule computes. Matches.
- Note, not a finding: `@objectstack/spec`'s own share of this diff is of kind `none` (an alias table growing, as #27745 and #27917 shipped at `patch`); a split changeset would have given spec `patch`. One changeset carries one kind, so `minor` is over-level, never under-level, and is accepted.
- `Clause-②:` line: `yes (widening)`. Right, per ① item 2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (not filed): `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` is still sent on a v2 GET; a v2 service ignores an unknown preference (RFC 7240 §2), and the `pageSize` describe and the guide say so. Accepted as a documented no-op; no card owed.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (not filed): the v2 fixtures are written from the services' published shape, not recorded live (no route to services.odata.org from the container); the fixture headers say so, as the v4 TripPin fixture's does. Accepted; the lane seat may file a live-recording follow-up when a networked run is available, at its discretion.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note owed.
- **Should-fix (lane seat, before ACCEPT; not a contract defect):** `Metadata-protocol: added` owes the PR body a third line, `Skills-docs: updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON` (pm-dispatch SKILL.md, the Metadata-protocol row). The PR body carries neither it nor a reason; the guide section in `content/docs/data-modeling/odata-datasources.mdx` is the likely `updated here` answer, but the line is the dev's to write from the diff.
- Check-runs on this head at review time: 43 in all; 18 concluded `success`, 5 concluded `skipped` (opt-in and matrix placeholders), none failed; 20 had not yet concluded: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped (query-options erasure; slot lookup & corpus; tooling self-tests), Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 through 8/8, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not stand in for them, and the Tier S landing condition (every check green) waits on them.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts` (the one `hits` file), against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against:

- **Key spelling holds end to end.** `parseCsdlV2` carries each `Property/@Type` verbatim after alias qualification (`Edm.DateTime`, `Edm.Time`); `introspectSchema` reports `p.type` as the column type (or `Collection(…)`); `canonicalizeSqlType` lower-cases and strips the parameter list, so `edm.datetime` / `edm.time` hit the new entries and `Collection(Edm.DateTime)` still reaches `collection` → `array`, as the comment above the arm says.
- **The rows match the driver's value shapes.** `readValue` yields an ISO UTC instant for `Edm.DateTime` and `HH:MM:SS[.f]` for `Edm.Time`; `writeValue` sends `/Date(ms)/` and `PT…S` back. The `datetime` row (`exact: ['datetime'], lossy: ['date']`) and the `time` row (`exact: ['time']`) describe exactly what a `datetime` / `time` / `date` field can hold of those values. The `date`-over-`Edm.DateTime` case the plugin-driver kit met ("temporal: every row, as stored") lands on `lossy`, which is the right verdict for a column that can carry midnight or any other time.
- **The comment is accurate.** [MC-CSDL] 2.0's primitives are Binary, Boolean, Byte, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, Decimal, Double, Guid, Int16, Int32, Int64, SByte, Single, String, Time; every one but the two added already sits in the arm under its v4 name, so "every other v2 primitive keeps its v4 name" is true, and `Edm.Time` "a time of day, written as a duration since midnight" is how v2 verbose JSON writes it.
- **Against the ruling it implements.** ADR-0015 §4.6's description of the `odata` arm is version-neutral and lists the deliberate exclusions (`Edm.Duration`, the Geo families); `Edm.DateTime` and `Edm.Time` were not among them, so mapping them closes a gap rather than opening one. No ADR amendment is owed, and none is in the diff, which is what keeps this PR off the Tier H register.
- **First consumer.** The head's service-datasource test drafts the v2 Northwind `Employees.BirthDate` (`Edm.DateTime`) as `datetime` with an empty review list apart from navigations, and Gate 2 passes over the same `$metadata` for five imported sets. `Edm.Time` has no consumer-level pin (Northwind declares none); it is pinned in `type-compat.test.ts` on both `canonicalizeSqlType` and `suggestFieldTypeForSqlType`, and exercised through the driver's in-process v2 service in the plugin-driver kit. Sufficient for a two-entry alias change.
- **Tried to break it.** `canonicalizeSqlType('Edm.DateTime')` with no dialect, or under `postgres`, stays `unknown` (the vocabulary remains the dialect's own, as the existing `Edm.Int32` pins require). The own-property guard on `DIALECT_ALIASES[dialect]` is unaffected by two more literal keys. `isCompatible` for every pair not naming the two types answers as on `main`: the diff adds keys and changes no existing entry or row.

No must-fix. No should-fix on the `hits` file. The one should-fix in ③ is a PR-body line for the lane seat's ACCEPT and does not touch the contract face.
